LESSON: READING 3.2.1 FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Transport Suggested vocabulary fly, float, road, rail, water, air, tarmac, fast,
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.2.1 Fluency, part of Transport Suggested vocabulary fly, float, road, rail, water, air, tarmac, fast, in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we read fluently?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. point out words from the print with appropriate font size with target letter- sound combinations (‘fl’, ‘ey’), while learners with blindness point out words from braille text with target letter- sound combinations (‘fl’, ‘ey’).

2. learners with low vision watch videos and learners with blindness listen to an audio recording or listen to the teacher model reading with fluency and say the words.

3. read aloud a print text for learners with low vision and braille text for learners with blindness at the benchmark level of 65 words per minute for learners with low vision and 35 words for learners with blindness, and pick out decodable and non- decodable words.

4. use word attack skills such as look and say or manipulate and say to recognise and read words related to the theme.

5. learners with low vision play word ladder and pronounce words or listen to audio/visual recording of words with letter sound correspondence, while learners with blindness are guided to play braille literacy games and pronounce words or listen to audio/visual recording of words with letter sound correspondence.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. point out words from the print with appropriate font size with target letter- sound combinations (‘fl’, ‘ey’), while learners with blindness point out words from braille text with target letter- sound combinations (‘fl’, ‘ey’).
2. learners with low vision watch videos and learners with blindness listen to an audio recording or listen to the teacher model reading with fluency and say the words.
3. read aloud a print text for learners with low vision and braille text for learners with blindness at the benchmark level of 65 words per minute for learners with low vision and 35 words for learners with blindness, and pick out decodable and non- decodable words.
4. use word attack skills such as look and say or manipulate and say to recognise and read words related to the theme.
5. learners with low vision play word ladder and pronounce words or listen to audio/visual recording of words with letter sound correspondence, while learners with blindness are guided to play braille literacy games and pronounce words or listen to audio/visual recording of words with letter sound correspondence.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.2.1 Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy; the learner’s interaction with digital devices with assistive technology is enhanced when they read digital texts.

Values:
Unity as the learner’s cooperation skills are enhanced as they work collaboratively with others during word games.

Pertinent Contemporary Issues:

Life Skills- self-esteem; the learner acquires an enhanced level of self-esteem as their reading fluency improves.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies reading fluency skills such as speed and accuracy in reading of texts.
